title: Unramified open locus of a representable stack morphism and its chartwise base change
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X\to\mathcal Y$ a morphism from an algebraic space to an algebraic stack over $S$, representable by algebraic spaces and locally of finite type. There is a largest open subspace $W_f\subset X$ such that $f|_{W_f}$ is unramified. For every morphism $g:\mathcal Y'\to\mathcal Y$ of algebraic stacks representable by algebraic spaces, put $X'=X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Y'$ with projection $p:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to\mathcal Y'$. The largest open subspace where $f'$ is unramified is $p^{-1}(W_f)$. If $\mathcal Y'=T$ is a scheme and $c:V\to X'$ is an etale scheme chart, then $c^{-1}p^{-1}(W_f)$ is exactly the union of the open subschemes of $V$ on which the composite $V\to T$ is unramified. A point of $V$ therefore belongs to this inverse image if and only if $V\to T$ is unramified on some open neighbourhood of that point. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. An algebraic stack is a stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre products and representability use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and smoothness uses [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Open subspaces are representable open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. Local finite type and unramifiedness are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism].

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:A\to\mathcal Y$. Put $U=X\times_{\mathcal Y}A$, $B=A\times_{\mathcal Y}A$, and $D=U\times_XU=X\times_{\mathcal Y}B$. Representability makes these algebraic spaces (for $B$, use the representable diagonal in the definition of algebraic stack). The projections $U\to X$ and $B\to A$ are smooth and surjective. The map $u:U\to A$ is locally of finite type. These assertions follow by base change and the atlas condition; the displayed identification is the associativity of the explicitly defined 2-fibre product. Let $O=U(u)\subset U$ be the largest unramified open, given by the algebraic-space locus lemma. Applied to each projection $B\to A$, its base-change equality says that both inverse images of $O$ in $D$ equal the same open $U(D\to B)$. Thus $O$ is invariant under the two projections $D\rightrightarrows U$.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), proof, atlas and invariant-open construction; Tag 06M5(3)

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $e:P\to U$. Then $q:P\to X$ is smooth and surjective. Put $O_P=e^{-1}(O)$. The map $P\times_XP\to U\times_XU$ and the invariance just proved give equality of the two inverse images of $O_P$. Apply invariant-open descent to the smooth scheme atlas $q$ of $X$: it gives an open substack $W\subset X$ with $P\times_XW=O_P$. This is an open subspace: the open-substack condition makes $W\to X$ representable by schemes (each scheme pullback is an open subscheme); applying representable pullback over the algebraic space $X$ to $W\to X$ and $X\to X$ shows that $W\simeq W\times_XX$ is an algebraic space. The two opens $U\times_XW$ and $O$ agree: their pullbacks to the etale cover $P\to U$ are $O_P$, and equality of open subfunctors is local for this cover, by the sheaf condition. Write $W_f=W$.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), proof, descent of the invariant open; Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation)

proof.text: The restriction $W_f\to\mathcal Y$ is representable: its scheme base changes are open subspaces of the corresponding base changes of $f$. Its base change to $A$ is $O\to A$, which is unramified. A smooth atlas is flat and locally finitely presented, so representable unramified descent implies that $W_f\to\mathcal Y$ is unramified. If $Z\subset X$ is any open subspace on which $f$ is unramified, its base change $Z_A\to A$ is unramified, by the defining scheme-base-change test. Thus $Z_A\subset O$ by maximality of $O$. Pulling back to $P$ gives $Z\times_XP\subset O_P$; the factorization criterion of invariant-open descent implies $Z\subset W_f$. This proves existence and maximality.

We verify the useful stronger chart identity $W_f\times_{\mathcal Y}T=U(X_T\to T)$ for every algebraic space $T\to\mathcal Y$, where $X_T=X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$. Put $C=A\times_{\mathcal Y}T$ and $E=X\times_{\mathcal Y}C$. These are algebraic spaces, and $C\to T$ is smooth surjective. The map $E\to C$ is the base change both of $U\to A$ along $C\to A$ and of $X_T\to T$ along $C\to T$. All three maps are locally of finite type. The space locus lemma identifies $U(E\to C)$ both with the inverse image of $O$ and with the inverse image of $U(X_T\to T)$. Since $U\times_XW_f=O$, the former is also the inverse image of $W_f\times_{\mathcal Y}T$. To descend this equality, choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $H\to E$. The composite $H\to X_T$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Both opens of $X_T$ have identical inverse images in $H$, so the inclusion-preserving bijection of invariant-open descent identifies them. This proves the formula without assuming $T\to\mathcal Y$ flat.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), proof of (B), filling out the chart comparison omitted there

proof.text: Now let $g:\mathcal Y^{\prime}\to\mathcal Y$ be representable as in the statement. Applying representable pullback to $g$ and the algebraic space $X$ shows that $X^{\prime}$ is an algebraic space. The base change $f^{\prime}$ is representable by associativity of scheme base changes, and is locally of finite type by base-change stability. Steps 1--3 therefore construct its largest unramified open $W_{f^{\prime}}$. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $A^{\prime}\to\mathcal Y^{\prime}$. Step 4, applied to $A^{\prime}\to\mathcal Y$ and to $A^{\prime}\to\mathcal Y^{\prime}$, identifies both $(p^{-1}W_f)\times_{\mathcal Y^{\prime}}A^{\prime}$ and $W_{f^{\prime}}\times_{\mathcal Y^{\prime}}A^{\prime}$ with $U(X^{\prime}\times_{\mathcal Y^{\prime}}A^{\prime}\to A^{\prime})$. Refining $X^{\prime}\times_{\mathcal Y^{\prime}}A^{\prime}\to X^{\prime}$ by an etale scheme atlas makes a smooth surjective scheme atlas of $X^{\prime}$. Invariant-open descent detects equality there and gives $W_{f^{\prime}}=p^{-1}W_f$.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), assertion (B), comparison after the atlas of the new target

proof.text: Finally take $\mathcal Y^{\prime}=T$ a scheme, and an etale scheme chart $c:V\to X^{\prime}$. Step 4 identifies $p^{-1}W_f$ with $L=U(f^{\prime})$. On $c^{-1}L$ the composite to $T$ is unramified, because $c$ is etale, hence unramified, and compositions of unramified space maps are unramified. Conversely, let $J\subset V$ be open with $J\to T$ unramified. The etale map $J\to X^{\prime}$ has an open image $I\subset X^{\prime}$ and $J\to I$ is surjective etale. In the compatible chart diagram for $I\to T$, take source $J\to I$ and target $T\to T$. The unramified chart criterion therefore implies that $I\to T$ is unramified, so $I\subset L$ by maximality. Consequently $J\subset c^{-1}L$. We have proved that $c^{-1}L$ is exactly the union of all such $J$. Membership in this union means precisely the existence of an open neighbourhood on which $V\to T$ is unramified, as required. This argument does not require the chart $c$ to be surjective.
